description: Raw Markdown mirror of every FilesHub documentation page. Each url returns the un-rendered .md (front matter included). Built for AI coding agents. See also /openapi.json.

files.title: About the author
files.description: FilesHub is built and maintained by Ahsan Mahmood, a senior full-stack engineer and the author of these docs.

files.title: Billing — buy a plan by card, and support FilesHub
files.description: Buy a FilesHub service plan by card through Polar with POST /api/v1/billing/checkout, how the plan switches on, renews, cancels and ends, and how to support FilesHub once or monthly.

files.title: Delete an object
files.description: DELETE /api/v1/objects/{public_id} permanently removes a FilesHub object — both the database record and the stored file. Requires a write-permission API key.

files.title: Recurring email schedules
files.description: Define cron-based recurring emails in FilesHub — create, list, update, pause, delete, and run-now — each sending to up to 50 recipients per run from a template or raw content.

files.title: Email templates
files.description: Manage reusable email templates in FilesHub — list them, and create, update, or delete them over the API — then send with template + variables.

files.title: Send an email
files.description: POST /api/v1/emails/send sends transactional email through FilesHub — raw HTML/text or a saved template, from one of three verified domains, queued by default with a job to poll.

files.title: Errors & limits
files.description: FilesHub returns a consistent JSON error envelope with an HTTP status code, and applies per-key rate limits and an upload size cap. This page lists every status code and limit.

files.title: Get / download an object
files.description: GET /api/v1/objects/{public_id} streams a stored file back from FilesHub. Public objects need no key; private objects require a read-permission key from the same project.

files.title: Job status
files.description: Poll GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} to track a queued FilesHub operation (like a queued email send) through queued → completed or failed, with attempts and result.

files.title: List objects
files.description: GET /api/v1/objects returns a paginated list of your project's stored files, newest first, with an optional visibility filter. Requires a read-permission API key.

files.title: OpenAPI spec (for AI agents & codegen)
files.description: FilesHub ships a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 spec at /openapi.json covering every API route — feed it to Claude Code, Codex, or an OpenAPI generator to integrate without guesswork.

files.title: API overview
files.description: The FilesHub API under /api/v1 covers file objects, transactional email, jobs, and 40+ developer utilities — all authenticated with an X-API-Key header. This page maps the contract.

files.title: Pagination
files.description: Every FilesHub list endpoint is paginated the same way — 20 rows by default, 50 maximum — and every response states its page, its total, how much remains, and the exact call to make next.

files.title: Password manager — access and scopes
files.description: How FilesHub decides which passwords an API key can reach — own and admin password scopes, every-project reach, the five abilities — and how to grant them in the dashboard or over the Management API with can_manage_passwords.

files.title: Password manager — using the dashboard
files.description: Manage FilesHub passwords by hand in the admin dashboard — add a login with a suggested strong password, see the password and current verification code, edit, delete and restore.

files.title: Password manager — endpoint reference
files.description: Every /api/v1/passwords endpoint — list, create, get, update, delete, restore, reveal and generate — with parameters, the ability each needs, request and response examples, and every error.

files.title: Password manager — overview
files.description: The FilesHub password manager stores logins per project — websites, usernames, encrypted passwords, verification codes, notes and tags — and lets API keys with an own or admin password scope create, read, reveal and manage them.

files.title: Password manager — quick start
files.description: Give a FilesHub API key a password scope, then create, find, reveal, change and delete a password over the API, with curl and JavaScript examples.

files.title: Security — how FilesHub protects your keys, files and passwords
files.description: How FilesHub protects stored credentials, API keys, files and passwords, which URLs it will fetch for you, the browser security headers, and two-step sign-in for the dashboard.

files.title: Verify a Turnstile token
files.description: POST /api/v1/turnstile/verify checks a Cloudflare Turnstile token using the secret key stored in your project's vault, so the secret never has to reach your frontend or a Cloudflare Worker.

files.title: Change an object's expiry or visibility
files.description: PATCH /api/v1/objects/{public_id} changes when a FilesHub object expires, or whether it is public or private, after upload. Requires a write-permission API key of the object's project.

files.title: Upload an object
files.description: POST /api/v1/objects uploads a multipart file to FilesHub and returns a 201 with the object's ULID, public URL, and metadata. Supports visibility and optional auto-expiry.

files.title: Developer utilities index
files.description: A summarized index of FilesHub's stateless developer-utility endpoint groups — converters, hashing, encoding, generators, and more — all under /api/v1 with an X-API-Key.

files.title: Version & health
files.description: GET /api/health and GET /api/version are FilesHub's public, no-auth status endpoints — health reports database connectivity, version returns the deployed backend build marker.

files.title: Changelog
files.description: Notable changes to the FilesHub documentation site, latest first.

files.title: Email marketing API
files.description: Endpoints for FilesHub email marketing — lists, contacts, paste and CSV imports, suppressions, sequences, enrollment, test sends, product events and the public subscribe form — on the data plane and the management plane.

files.title: Contact batches
files.description: Each imported CSV becomes one numbered batch in the shared people pool. A batch is given to one product's campaign at a time, never to the same product twice, and every use is recorded with its results.

files.title: Contact cleaning
files.description: How FilesHub checks every address in the shared contact pool before a campaign mails it — address rules, DNS, an AI review of company domains, bounce history and a mailbox check with the recipient's own server — and how a project paused for bounces resumes by itself.

files.title: The gap between campaigns
files.description: A person who received a campaign email gets no email from a different campaign for 20 days. Follow-ups of a campaign already running for that person keep their own timing.

files.title: Mailbox warm-up and deliverability
files.description: How FilesHub warms up every sending mailbox with persona conversations, measures real replies, tunes each mailbox's daily limit every night, and exposes the numbers and controls on the Management API.

files.title: Email marketing overview
files.description: FilesHub email marketing keeps per-project contact lists, imports contacts by CSV, paste or one at a time, and sends drip sequences that branch on clicks and product events — with consent, suppression and one-click unsubscribe built in.

files.title: The shared people pool
files.description: One pool of people for the whole FilesHub account — a contact imported once can join a list of any project without a second upload, with one history per person across products.

files.title: Connect your product to email marketing
files.description: The recipe every product follows to connect FilesHub email marketing — carry the ?c= contact token through sign-up, report signed_up and activated events from the server, and add a double opt-in form.

files.title: Send log and campaign report
files.description: Which email went to whom, from which campaign, step and mailbox, and what happened after — plus the stored campaign report with the waiting queue and a forecast date.

files.title: FAQ
files.description: Frequently asked questions about FilesHub — what it is, how to authenticate, public vs private files, size limits, SDKs, deleting files, and how it compares to S3 or Firebase Storage.

files.title: API key restrictions (ship a key in a frontend)
files.description: Restrict a FilesHub API key to your own web origins, browser-extension ids, Android package + signing certificate, or iOS bundle id — so you can embed the key in a React/mobile/extension app without a proxy backend.

files.title: Authentication
files.description: FilesHub authenticates every request with an X-API-Key header. Keys are per project, carry read and write permissions, and can be restricted to specific web origins or mobile app ids.

files.title: File visibility (public vs private)
files.description: Each FilesHub object is public or private. Public objects are downloadable by anyone at their URL; private objects require a read-permission API key from the same project.

files.title: Quick Start
files.description: Upload your first file to FilesHub in about five minutes — get an API key, POST a multipart file with your X-API-Key, and use the returned public URL.

files.title: Browser & mobile uploads
files.description: How to upload to FilesHub safely from a browser or a mobile app — multipart form data, restricted keys scoped to your domain or bundle id, and the backend-proxy alternative.

files.title: Integrate from any app
files.description: Copy-paste FilesHub integration for JavaScript/TypeScript, React, PHP/Laravel, and mobile — upload a file, store the returned URL, render it, and clean it up on delete.

files.title: Introduction
files.description: FilesHub is a file-storage and developer-utility API — upload a file over HTTP with an X-API-Key header, get a stable public URL, then list, download, or delete it.

files.title: Agent workflow — auto-configure a project's API key
files.description: Step-by-step recipe for an AI coding agent to map a local project to its FilesHub project and enforce origin restrictions on its API key using the Management API, checking global origins before adding duplicates.

files.title: Amplitude accounts
files.description: Record which Amplitude account holds which project, how many projects each account may hold, which FilesHub project each Amplitude project measures, and its API key, over the FilesHub Management API.

files.title: Management API authentication
files.description: Authenticate the FilesHub Management API with an fh_pat_ access token via the Authorization Bearer header, and understand token scope, expiry, and revocation.

files.title: Credential checks ("Test Analytics")
files.description: Send a real "Test Analytics" event to a project's Firebase Analytics, GA4, Amplitude and Sentry — or verify the stored credentials read-only — per project and per tool, from the Management API, with an honest verdict for each.

files.title: Debug keystores
files.description: Every build machine's Android debug signing key on one account-level record — SHA-1 and SHA-256 fingerprints readable without a reveal, the keystore file itself backed up, and a derived block on every project's vault payload.

files.title: Developer accounts
files.description: Store the tokens that publish under your name — npm, Hugging Face, Docker Hub, PyPI, crates.io, the extension stores, Vercel, Netlify, Sentry — on one account-level record, and read them back over the FilesHub Management API with a ready-to-write .npmrc line.

files.title: Management API endpoints
files.description: Full endpoint reference for the FilesHub Public Management API — access tokens, projects, API keys (create, rotate, reveal), origins, global origins, and reverse key lookup, with request and response examples.

files.title: Google OAuth clients and keep-alive
files.description: Import every Google OAuth client a project owns from Firebase, google-services.json and Supabase, and keep each one in use daily so Google never deletes it as unused.

files.title: Management API overview
files.description: The FilesHub Public Management API lets a trusted server or AI coding agent create projects, mint and rotate per-project API keys, configure origin restrictions, and read a project's stored credentials using one account-wide access token.

files.title: Payment accounts
files.description: Keep the API keys, webhook secrets and login details of your payment-provider accounts (Stripe, PayPal, Polar.sh, Creem, Lemon Squeezy, Paddle and more) on one record, and read them back over the FilesHub Management API.

files.title: Project vault
files.description: Store every third-party credential, config file and identifier a project needs — Firebase, Google Cloud, Sentry, OneSignal, Cloudflare, store consoles, signing keys and more — and read, reveal AND write them over the FilesHub Management API with a scoped token, including ready-to-paste .env blocks.

files.title: Supabase account tokens
files.description: Read a Supabase account's personal access token (sbp_…) over the FilesHub Management API, behind its own can_read_supabase_tokens scope, plus the SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN env line the Supabase CLI reads.

files.title: Supabase project vault
files.description: Read and reveal a Supabase project's full credential set — API keys, JWT secret, Postgres connection details, and S3 keys — over the FilesHub Management API, plus ready-to-paste React, Node and Laravel .env blocks.

files.title: Platform services (beyond storage)
files.description: Beyond file storage, FilesHub exposes 50+ stateless developer-utility endpoints on the same base URL and X-API-Key — hashing, encoding, converters, QR codes, short URLs, OTP, a vault, and image/PDF processing.

files.title: Privacy
files.description: Privacy notice for the FilesHub documentation site and the FilesHub API — what the docs site collects, what the API stores, and how to get data removed.
